title: America's newest super weapon sparks claims US has lied about UFOs
text:
By CHRIS MELORE, US DEPUTY SCIENCE EDITOR

Published:  03:57 AEST, 15 September 2026   |  Updated:  14:37 AEST, 15 September 2026

One of the world’s largest defense and aerospace companies has unveiled a new type of military aircraft after sparking wild theories that the US was now using UFO technology.

On Monday, Lockheed Martin revealed its secret unmanned combat drone called Vectis. The large, remote-controlled stealth plane is expected to travel with US jets, fighting alongside military pilots.

Prior to the unveiling at a major Air Force conference in Washington, DC, Lockheed released a cryptic message showing the silhouette of an unknown craft, claiming that the 'next level' had been 'unlocked' by its top-secret division called Skunk Works.

Many who saw the post on social media immediately began to claim without evidence that the defense contractor was still hiding other designs which had been reverse-engineered using parts from crashed UFOs.

One person said: 'Now let’s see the reverse-engineered craft.' Another added: 'Now show us the antigravity craft you’ve been hiding from the public for the past 70 years.'

Despite claims by former CIA scientists and other military whistleblowers, the Pentagon and White House have maintained that no physical evidence of UFOs has ever been recovered.

According to Lockheed, five Vectis drones will be created by 2027, providing the US military with a revolutionary aircraft that can fight other fighter planes, bomb ground targets or secretly gather intelligence as a spy plane.

While onlookers at Lockheed's futuristic combat drone may not have any proof that Vectis was inspired by UFOs, at least one former employee for the defense contractor has claimed those rumors are true.

On September 12, defense contractor Lockheed Martin released a cryptic message that many believed was hinting at an aircraft using UFO technology

On September 14, Lockheed unveiled a full-scale model and video of the Vectis, a new unmanned combat drone

Boyd Bushman, a former Lockheed Martin and Texas Instruments engineer who died in 2014, publicly claimed he had worked with UFOs and aliens to reverse engineer spacecraft '24 hours a day.'

During his deathbed confession, Bushman even revealed a stack of photographs he alleged were of extraterrestrials he worked with on the secret projects at Area 51 in the Nevada desert.

'They're approximately five feet four inches to five feet tall,' Bushman said, as he held up images of what he touted as a real alien lifeform.

Bushman's claims have never been verified, and skeptics claim his photos appeared to show commercially available prop dolls sold online.

Lockheed has rarely commented on claims that its secret research divisions have any ties to potentially extraterrestrial materials, with a spokesman telling reporters in 2023: 'Questions about UAPs are best addressed by the US government.'

The defense contractor is best known for creating the F-35 fighter jet, the F-22 Raptor and the C-130 transport plane.

Its Skunk Works division, which was founded in 1943, has been tasked with developing cutting-edge aircraft quickly and quietly for decades.

On Monday, Lockheed claimed that the Vectis unmanned fighters would 'deliver a new level of lethality, survivability, adaptability and operational flexibility for America and its allies.'

Lockheed Martin revealed the new aircraft at a major Air Force conference in Washington

Conspiracy theorists have claimed that the Vectis is a piece of reverse engineered technology using recovered UFOs

Its space-age aircraft has a tailless, flying-wing design, boosting its stealth ability and lowering the drag normal fighter jets experience.

The Vectis also has a hidden engine intake on top of its body, making it harder for enemy radar to detect.

The unmanned craft is roughly 34 feet long with a 38-foot wingspan, about the same length as an MQ-9 Reaper drone and similar in wingspan to the F-35.

With less drag from extra fins and flaps sticking out, Vectis will be able to carry bigger payloads of weapons, which are also kept inside the craft until launched.

Despite touting their new drone's game-changing advancements, skeptics continued to claim Lockheed was still holding back after their announcement in Washington.

'Release the Alien Reproduction Vehicles, we know you produce them,' one person replied to Lockheed's announcement on X.

'Quite an alien-looking design,' another social media user claimed.

Boyd Bushman sat down with independent aerospace engineer Mark Q Patterson shortly before he died at age 78 on August 17, 2014, where he revealed a stack of photographs he said were of extraterrestrials

Bushman, a former Lockheed Martin employee, claimed that his people inside Area 51 sent him pictures of not only alien bodies, but also UFOs being held at the base

In recent days, satellite images have also captured new drone designs at a secret base in Asia, known as China's Area 51.

Documentary director Dan Farah said that several US officials, including Secretary of State Marco Rubio and former Director of National Intelligence James Clapper, believed the world was now locked in a new Cold War to reengineer the alien technology recovered from these ships.

Air Force veteran-turned-whistleblower David Grusch and former CIA scientist Dr Hal Puthoff have both claimed that the US government has been running a secret UFO recovery program since the 1940s, which has taken control of at least ten extraterrestrial craft.

According to Lockheed, the drone unveiled on Monday was only a full-scale model of the Vectis. The first full-scale prototype is expected to be delivered to the military by the end of 2027.
